official_title.value: A Multi-Center, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo- and Active Comparator-Controlled Phase 3 Study With Randomized Withdrawal and Retreatment to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of BMS-986165 in Subjects With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis

mechanism_of_action.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/label mechanism_of_action (FDA-approved label, section 12.1) -- v1 extracted text: 12.1 Mechanism of Action Deucravacitinib is an inhibitor of tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2). TYK2 is a member of the Janus kinase (JAK) family. Deucravacitinib binds to the regulatory domain of TYK2, stabilizing an inhibitory interaction between the regulatory and the catalytic domains of the enzyme. This results in allosteric inhibition of receptor-mediated activation of TYK2 and its downstream activation of Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription (STATs) as shown in cell-based assays. JAK kinases, including TYK2, function as pairs of homo- or heterodimers in the JAK-STAT pathways. TYK2 pairs with JAK1 to mediate multiple cytokine pathways and also pairs with JAK2 to transmit signals as shown in cell-based assays. The precise mechanism linking inhibition of TYK2 enzyme to treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis or active psoriatric arthritis is not currently known.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 6.7.1 Prohibited and/or Restricted Treatments: lists exposure to other investigational drugs, strong CYP450 inducers, medications aggravating psoriasis, opioid analgesics, phototherapy, biologic medications, oral psoriasis medications, oral/injectable corticosteroids (with otic/ophthalmic/nasal/inhaled exception), topical medications affecting psoriasis evaluation, medicated shampoos, and live vaccination as prohibited/restricted. Section 6.7.2 Permitted Concomitant Medications: "Stable doses of concomitant medication for chronic medical conditions, except for psoriasis, are permitted... Low potency topical steroids (WHO Classes VI and VII) are permitted on the palms, soles, face, and intertriginous areas... Bland emollients... are allowed on all body regions."

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Testing Strategy for Efficacy Endpoints: "The primary family of coprimary endpoints will each be tested at a Type I error =0.05 first and, if significant for both endpoints, testing will proceed for the secondary family of key secondary endpoints. The primary family of coprimary endpoints will be the serial gatekeeper for proceeding with testing of the secondary family of key secondary efficacy endpoints. Primary Family - Coprimary endpoints compared with placebo; both must be significant at a Type I error=0.05... Primary 1: Proportion of subjects who achieve sPGA 0/1 at Week 16; Primary 2: Proportion of subjects who achieve PASI 75 at Week 16. In order to control for Type I error rate inflation within the secondary family of key secondary endpoints, separate testing branches with a 2-sided Type I error=0.025 will be used for comparisons of BMS-986165 6 mg QD compared to placebo and BMS-986165 6 mg QD compared to apremilast. A hierarchical testing method within each testing branch will be implemented."

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Section 1.1 Overall Design: "This will be a 52-week, multi-center, randomized double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active comparator-controlled study... Subjects will undergo screening evaluations within 28 days prior to administration of study medication... At Week 16, subjects receiving placebo will be switched in a blinded manner to BMS-986165 6 mg QD... At Week 24, subjects originally randomized to BMS-986165 6 mg QD who do not achieve PASI 75 response will continue to receive BMS-986165 6 mg QD... Subjects who achieve PASI 75 response will enter the randomized withdrawal and maintenance period." And later: "The coprimary endpoints will be evaluated at Week 16. The duration of the study for each subject will be up to 52 weeks on treatment, and 4 additional weeks for safety follow-up."

maintenance_period_rule.topical_rescue: At Week 24 only, a subject with sPGA>=3 may be treated with restricted topicals (high potency corticosteroids WHO Classes I-V, >3% salicylic acid, urea, alpha-/beta-hydroxyl acids, anthralin, calcipotriene, vitamin D derivatives, retinoids, tazarotene) or medicated shampoos (containing corticosteroids, coal tar, >3% salicylic acid, or vitamin D3 analogues), at investigator discretion, usable as needed through Week 52; cannot be initiated at any later time point.
maintenance_period_rule.systemic_rescue: During the randomized withdrawal/maintenance period (Weeks 24-52), Week-24 PASI75 responders re-randomized to placebo (and apremilast-arm PASI75 responders switched to placebo) who relapse (>=50% loss of Week 24 PASI percent improvement from baseline) are switched to BMS-986165 6mg QD until the end of the maintenance period (Week 52). Apremilast-arm PASI75 non-responders at Week 24 are also switched to BMS-986165 6mg QD.

value.topical_agent_class: high potency corticosteroids (WHO Classes I-V) and other restricted topicals/medicated shampoos
value.rationale: POETYK PSO-1 has two distinct rescue mechanisms: (1) a topical/shampoo escape restricted to a single Week-24 initiation window for sPGA>=3 nonresponders, and (2) a systemic relapse-triggered switch back to active drug (BMS-986165 6mg QD) for re-randomized-to-placebo responders during the Week 24-52 randomized withdrawal period.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 6.7.3 Rescue Medications: "At Week 24, a subject who has an sPGA [>=3] may be treated with restricted topicals or shampoos, respectively, at the investigator's discretion (see Section 6.7.1). These treatments may be only initiated at Week 24, and not at subsequent time points." (sPGA threshold recovered from Section 1.1 Overall Design: "Any subject with sPGA >= 3 at Week 24 may be treated with restricted topical medications, such as topical high potency corticosteroids (WHO Classes I-V), only at this time point at the discretion of the investigator.") Section 1.1: "If the subjects re-randomized to placebo experience a relapse as defined below at any visit during this period, they will be treated with BMS-986165 6 mg QD until the end of the maintenance period (Week 52)... relapse will be defined as at least a 50% loss of Week 24 PASI percent improvement from baseline."
